title: Model pinning and reproducibility
summary: Recording the exact dated model snapshot used, rather than a floating alias that silently changes.
what: Providers expose both moving aliases and dated snapshots. An alias resolves to whatever is current at call time.
why: If a judge sets a published number, a floating reference means re-running months later silently uses a different judge, and the number moves with no explanation in the output.
how: Resolve the alias to its snapshot at run start and record that, not the name that was requested.
in_this_project: Verified against the provider's model list: a -latest alias reports a floating label as its version, while a dated model reports a snapshot. Every query and judgment records name@snapshot, and a run config captures both model references, the candidate depth, the batch size, the seed and the corpus file.

advantages: The judge behind a published number is identifiable

pitfalls: Using a -latest alias anywhere a number is published
Recording the requested name rather than the resolved snapshot

use: Any model call whose output becomes a published figure
